title: Which NREFT operators can produce a lone high-energy recoil? Spectral shape ratios in xenon and a reproduction of the LZ signal spectra
question: For O1,O3-O15 (s,v; 200/1000/4000 GeV) what is R(200-270 keV)/R(5.4-55 keV), how many low-energy events accompany one high-energy event, and which operators survive the 2024 low-energy null? What WimPyDD coupling reproduces LZ Fig. 1?
headline_result: Only q^2-suppressed spin operators O6 (N_lo=0.43), O5v (1.05), O15 (0.75-1.9), O9 (2.1), O14 (2.3), O10 (3.1) give <=5 low-energy events per 200-270 keV event at >=1 TeV; O1 (2752), O11 (258), O8s (156), O12 (41-100), O7 (32-36), O4 (28) are excluded. LZ unit coupling c=1/m_v^2 (Anand) = WimPyDD c0=2/m_v^2 (WimPyDD c0=cp+cn; factor 4 in rate), reproduced to 1-3% below 60 keV.
key_numbers: WimPyDD(2/m_v^2)/Fig1 = 1.012 (10 keV), 1.028 (50), 0.90 (150), 0.88 (250); N_lo(1000 GeV) O1s 2752, O1v 477, O4 28, O10 3.1, O9 2.1, O6 0.43, O5v 1.05, O15v 0.75; inelastic O1s N_lo 501/7.6/0 at delta 100/200/300 keV; L10 ~ (q^2/mN^2)O4-O6 pure q^4 Sigma', dip 52 vs 61 keV, rms 0.086 dex, N_lo 0.20 vs 0.155 (digitised); M-response minima 100.4 vs 102 keV and ~265 keV
model_or_mechanism: NREFT (Fitzpatrick/Anand) spin-1/2 WIMP, elastic O1,O3-O15 s/v; magnetic-dipole-like L10 combination; inelastic O1 reference
confidence: high for normalisation and operator ordering; medium for the compatible/excluded boundary (depends on recalled 2024 tolerance N_max~3-5)
agent_tools: Read 10, Bash 14, Write 5, Edit 17, ToolSearch 2, TaskStop 2
software_and_packages: python 3.12.13; WimPyDD 2.0.4 (eft_hamiltonian incl. q-dependent WC, diff_rate, streamed_halo_function); pymupdf 1.28.2; numpy 2.5.3; scipy 1.18.1; pandas 3.0.5; matplotlib 3.11.2; common/lzcommon.py
local_inputs: Fig1_combined_recoils.pdf (vector paths); fulltext.tex Theory/Fig.1 caption, Data Analysis, LEE section, Tables S6-S7; dossier; lzcommon.py
recalled_knowledge: 8 items: NREFT operator responses (certain), Anand c0=(cp+cn)/2 (likely), 2024 LZ tolerance ~3-5 events (uncertain), L1/L5->O1, L2->O10, L3->O11, L4->O6, L15->O4 (likely), L10 reduction (likely), (Z-N)/A (certain), arXiv 2410.17036 (likely)
